# Subway Seat for PowerShell

Command-line colors in PSReadLine, the same as the fish port: gold commands, orange keywords and pipes, sage parameters and types, avocado strings, terracotta variables. On PowerShell 7.2+ it also sets $PSStyle, so tables, errors, progress bars and Get-ChildItem listings (gold directories) match. Keys an older PSReadLine doesn't know are skipped. The terminal's own colors come from your terminal's port.

[PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/) · [Previews and copy buttons](https://oddurs.github.io/subway-seat/ports/powershell/) · Needs PSReadLine 2.0+

## Turn it on

**Subway Seat**, in your profile ($PROFILE: ~/.config/powershell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1 on macOS and Linux, Documents\PowerShell\ on Windows):

```powershell
. "$PSScriptRoot/subway-seat.ps1"
```

**Subway Seat Tunnel**, in your profile ($PROFILE: ~/.config/powershell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1 on macOS and Linux, Documents\PowerShell\ on Windows):

```powershell

```

**Subway Seat Enamel**, in your profile ($PROFILE: ~/.config/powershell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1 on macOS and Linux, Documents\PowerShell\ on Windows):

## Follow light and dark

In your profile, instead of the line above (picks a flavor from the system appearance when PowerShell starts; Linux stays dark):

```powershell
$dark = $true
if ($IsMacOS) { $dark = (defaults read -g AppleInterfaceStyle 2>$null) -eq 'Dark' }
elseif ($IsWindows -or $PSVersionTable.PSEdition -eq 'Desktop') {
    $dark = (Get-ItemPropertyValue 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize' AppsUseLightTheme -ErrorAction Ignore) -ne 1
}
. "$PSScriptRoot/$(if ($dark) { 'subway-seat' } else { 'subway-seat-enamel' }).ps1"
```

## Uninstall

- Delete `~/.config/powershell/subway-seat.ps1`.
- Delete `~/.config/powershell/subway-seat-tunnel.ps1`.
- Delete `~/.config/powershell/subway-seat-enamel.ps1`.
- Delete `~/.config/powershell/london-moquette.ps1`.
- Delete `~/.config/powershell/london-deep-level.ps1`.
- Delete `~/.config/powershell/london-portland.ps1`.
- Remove the line you added to turn it on.
